html:
SMTO-PSM-0025 — SMTO can't turn a saved parameter into a different kind

GUID: 7682daad-333e-5e79-9709-26cebc908a7a
Slug: parameter-profile-type-change
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: parameters

What happened

  • The Agent tried to edit a saved parameter in a way that would turn it into a different kind of profile, for example from a server connection into something else. SMTO refused, and the parameter was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and select the parameter the Agent was editing to confirm it still has its original contents. This confirms the refused edit left the parameter exactly as it was.
  2. To get a different kind of profile, pick the matching template in the list next to the New button, select New, fill it in, and select Save. Each kind of profile has its own template, and a new parameter avoids breaking tasks that use the old one.
  3. In your messages, mention the new parameter with @ instead of the old one. The Agent then works with the profile of the kind you need.

What success looks like

  • The new parameter appears in the Parameter Store list, and the original parameter is unchanged.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to keep retrying the same change; delete the old parameter yourself only once nothing uses it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The parameters.patch tool rejected a change because it would alter the stored record's profile_type; no write was made.

What this means

  • The patch attempts to change the saved profile type. The classification describes only the condition observed by the producer.

Why this can happen

  • A patch changes profile_type relative to the retained record.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • parameters.patch (agent_runtime/skills/parameters/patch.py) forbids changing profile_type and returns a non-executed receipt. Create a new parameter from the correct template, or perform an explicit full replacement of the record against its current updated_at revision after confirming the intended replacement.
  • Use the explicit full-replacement operation to change profile type, retaining the current revision and confirming the intended replacement.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
